audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Kings / Melakhim Aleph chapter 20, first-pass draft aligned to public-domain verse structure; formal military-history and witness audit remains required.
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for siege, wives and children as demanded property, palace search, intoxication context, youth deployment, mass casualties, hill/valley religious stereotyping, wall collapse, prisoner negotiation, royal mercy, treaty, coerced prophetic injury, lion death, disguise, herem language, and condemnation of released captive.

verses.restored: Ben-hadad king of Aram gathered all his army; thirty-two kings were with him, with horses and chariots. He went up, besieged Samaria, and fought against it.

familiar.text: And Benhadad the king of Syria gathered all his host together: and there were thirty and two kings with him, and horses, and chariots; and he went up and besieged Samaria, and warred against it.

modern.text: Now Ben-hadad king of Aram assembled his entire army. Accompanied by thirty-two kings with their horses and chariots, he marched up, besieged Samaria, and waged war against it.

original.text: וּבֶן הֲדַ֣ד מֶֽלֶךְ אֲרָ֗ם קָבַץ֙ אֶת כָּל חֵיל֔וֹ וּשְׁלֹשִׁ֨ים וּשְׁנַ֥יִם מֶ֛לֶךְ אִתּ֖וֹ וְס֣וּס וָרָ֑כֶב וַיַּ֗עַל וַיָּ֨צַר֙ עַל שֹׁ֣מְר֔וֹן וַיִּלָּ֖חֶם בָּֽהּ

verses.restored: He sent messengers into city to Ahab king of Israel and said to him, Thus says Ben-hadad:

familiar.text: And he sent messengers to Ahab king of Israel into the city, and said unto him, Thus saith Benhadad,

modern.text: Then he sent messengers into the city to Ahab king of Israel,

original.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֧ח מַלְאָכִ֛ים אֶל אַחְאָ֥ב מֶֽלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל הָעִֽירָה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֗וֹ כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר בֶּן הֲדַ֔ד

verses.restored: Your silver and gold are mine; your wives and your children, the best, are mine.

familiar.text: Thy silver and thy gold is mine; thy wives also and thy children, even the goodliest, are mine.

modern.text: saying, “This is what Ben-hadad says: ‘Your silver and gold are mine, and your best wives and children are mine!’”

original.text: כַּסְפְּךָ֥ וּֽזְהָבְךָ֖ לִֽי ה֑וּא וְנָשֶׁ֧יךָ וּבָנֶ֛יךָ הַטּוֹבִ֖ים לִי הֵֽם

verses.restored: King of Israel answered, According to your word, my lord the king, I am yours and all I have.

familiar.text: And the king of Israel answered and said, My lord, O king, according to thy saying, I am thine, and all that I have.

modern.text: And the king of Israel replied, “Just as you say, my lord the king: I am yours, along with all that I have.”

original.text: וַיַּ֤עַן מֶֽלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וַיֹּ֔אמֶר כִּדְבָרְךָ֖ אֲדֹנִ֣י הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ לְךָ֥ אֲנִ֖י וְכָל אֲשֶׁר לִֽי

verses.restored: Messengers returned and said, Thus says Ben-hadad: Though I sent to you, saying, Give me your silver, gold, wives, and children,

familiar.text: And the messengers came again, and said, Thus speaketh Benhadad, saying, Although I have sent unto thee, saying, Thou shalt deliver me thy silver, and thy gold, and thy wives, and thy children;

modern.text: The messengers came back and said, “This is what Ben-hadad says: ‘I have sent to you to demand your silver, your gold, your wives, and your children.

original.text: וַיָּשֻׁ֨בוּ֙ הַמַּלְאָכִ֔ים וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ כֹּֽה אָמַ֥ר בֶּן הֲדַ֖ד לֵאמֹ֑ר כִּֽי שָׁלַ֤חְתִּי אֵלֶ֨יךָ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר כַּסְפְּךָ֧ וּזְהָבְךָ֛ וְנָשֶׁ֥יךָ וּבָנֶ֖יךָ לִ֥י תִתֵּֽן

verses.restored: tomorrow at this time I will send my servants to search your house and houses of your servants. Everything desirable in your eyes they shall place in their hands and take.

familiar.text: Yet I will send my servants unto thee to morrow about this time, and they shall search thine house, and the houses of thy servants; and it shall be, that whatsoever is pleasant in thine eyes, they shall put it in their hand, and take it away.

modern.text: But about this time tomorrow I will send my servants to search your palace and the houses of your servants. They will seize and carry away all that is precious to you.’”

original.text: כִּ֣י אִם כָּעֵ֣ת מָחָ֗ר אֶשְׁלַ֤ח אֶת עֲבָדַי֙ אֵלֶ֔יךָ וְחִפְּשׂוּ֙ אֶת בֵּ֣יתְךָ֔ וְאֵ֖ת בָּתֵּ֣י עֲבָדֶ֑יךָ וְהָיָה֙ כָּל מַחְמַ֣ד עֵינֶ֔יךָ יָשִׂ֥ימוּ בְיָדָ֖ם וְלָקָֽחוּ

verses.restored: King of Israel called all elders of land and said, Please know and see this one seeks evil. He sent for my wives, children, silver, and gold, and I did not withhold from him.

familiar.text: Then the king of Israel called all the elders of the land, and said, Mark, I pray you, and see how this man seeketh mischief: for he sent unto me for my wives, and for my children, and for my silver, and for my gold; and I denied him not.

modern.text: Then the king of Israel summoned all the elders of the land and said, “Please take note and see that this man is looking for trouble, for when he demanded my wives, my children, my silver, and my gold, I did not deny him.”

original.text: וַיִּקְרָ֤א מֶֽלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לְכָל זִקְנֵ֣י הָאָ֔רֶץ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ דְּעֽוּ נָ֣א וּרְא֔וּ כִּ֥י רָעָ֖ה זֶ֣ה מְבַקֵּ֑שׁ כִּֽי שָׁלַ֨ח אֵלַ֜י לְנָשַׁ֤י וּלְבָנַי֙ וּלְכַסְפִּ֣י וְלִזְהָבִ֔י וְלֹ֥א מָנַ֖עְתִּי מִמֶּֽנּוּ

verses.restored: All elders and all people said to him, Do not listen and do not consent.

familiar.text: And all the elders and all the people said unto him, Hearken not unto him, nor consent.

modern.text: And the elders and the people all said, “Do not listen to him or consent to his terms.”

original.text: וַיֹּאמְר֥וּ אֵלָ֛יו כָּל הַזְּקֵנִ֖ים וְכָל הָעָ֑ם אַל תִּשְׁמַ֖ע וְל֥וֹא תֹאבֶֽה

verses.restored: He said to messengers of Ben-hadad, Say to my lord the king: All you sent to your servant at first I will do, but this matter I cannot do. Messengers went and returned word.

familiar.text: Wherefore he said unto the messengers of Benhadad, Tell my lord the king, All that thou didst send for to thy servant at the first I will do: but this thing I may not do. And the messengers departed, and brought him word again.

modern.text: So Ahab answered the messengers of Ben-hadad, “Tell my lord the king, ‘All that you demanded of your servant the first time I will do, but this thing I cannot do.’” So the messengers departed and relayed the message to Ben-hadad.

original.text: וַיֹּ֜אמֶר לְמַלְאֲכֵ֣י בֶן הֲדַ֗ד אִמְר֞וּ לַֽאדֹנִ֤י הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ כֹּל֩ אֲשֶׁר שָׁלַ֨חְתָּ אֶל עַבְדְּךָ֤ בָרִֽאשֹׁנָה֙ אֶעֱשֶׂ֔ה וְהַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה לֹ֥א אוּכַ֖ל לַעֲשׂ֑וֹת וַיֵּֽלְכוּ֙ הַמַּלְאָכִ֔ים וַיְשִׁבֻ֖הוּ דָּבָֽר

verses.restored: Ben-hadad sent to him: Thus may gods do to me and thus add, if dust of Samaria is enough for handfuls for all people at my feet.

familiar.text: And Benhadad sent unto him, and said, The gods do so unto me, and more also, if the dust of Samaria shall suffice for handfuls for all the people that follow me.

modern.text: Then Ben-hadad sent another message to Ahab: “May the gods deal with me, and ever so severely, if enough dust remains of Samaria for each of my men to have a handful.”

original.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח אֵלָיו֙ בֶּן הֲדַ֔ד וַיֹּ֕אמֶר כֹּֽה יַעֲשׂ֥וּן לִ֛י אֱלֹהִ֖ים וְכֹ֣ה יוֹסִ֑פוּ אִם יִשְׂפֹּק֙ עֲפַ֣ר שֹׁמְר֔וֹן לִשְׁעָלִ֕ים לְכָל הָעָ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּרַגְלָֽי

verses.restored: King of Israel answered, Speak: Let one girding on armor not boast like one taking it off.

familiar.text: And the king of Israel answered and said, Tell him, Let not him that girdeth on his harness boast himself as he that putteth it off.

modern.text: And the king of Israel replied, “Tell him: ‘The one putting on his armor should not boast like one taking it off.’”

original.text: וַיַּ֤עַן מֶֽלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר דַּבְּר֔וּ אַל יִתְהַלֵּ֥ל חֹגֵ֖ר כִּמְפַתֵּֽחַ

verses.restored: When Ben-hadad heard this word, he and kings were drinking in shelters. He said to servants, Set yourselves. They set themselves against city.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, when Ben-hadad heard this message, as he was drinking, he and the kings in the pavilions, that he said unto his servants, Set yourselves in array. And they set themselves in array against the city.

modern.text: Ben-hadad received this message while he and the kings were drinking in their tents, and he said to his servants, “Take your positions.” So they stationed themselves against the city. Ahab Defeats Ben-hadad

original.text: וַיְהִ֗י כִּשְׁמֹ֨עַ֙ אֶת הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה וְה֥וּא שֹׁתֶ֛ה ה֥וּא וְהַמְּלָכִ֖ים בַּסֻּכּ֑וֹת וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֶל עֲבָדָיו֙ שִׂ֔ימוּ וַיָּשִׂ֖ימוּ עַל הָעִֽיר

verses.restored: Look, a prophet came near Ahab king of Israel and said, Thus says YHWH: Have you seen all this great multitude? Look, I am giving it into your hand this day, and you shall know I am YHWH.

familiar.text: And, behold, there came a prophet unto Ahab king of Israel, saying, Thus saith the LORD, Hast thou seen all this great multitude? behold, I will deliver it into thine hand this day; and thou shalt know that I am the LORD.

modern.text: Meanwhile a prophet approached Ahab king of Israel and declared, “This is what the LORD says: ‘Do you see this entire great army? Behold, I will deliver it into your hand this very day, and you will know that I am the LORD.’”

original.text: וְהִנֵּ֣ה נָבִ֣יא אֶחָ֗ד נִגַּשׁ֮ אֶל אַחְאָ֣ב מֶֽלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל֒ וַיֹּ֗אמֶר כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הְֽרָאִ֔יתָ אֵ֛ת כָּל הֶהָמ֥וֹן הַגָּד֖וֹל הַזֶּ֑ה הִנְנִ֨י נֹתְנ֤וֹ בְיָֽדְךָ֙ הַיּ֔וֹם וְיָדַעְתָּ֖ כִּֽי אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: Ahab said, By whom? He said, Thus says YHWH: By young men of provincial officials. He said, Who shall begin battle? He said, You.

familiar.text: And Ahab said, By whom? And he said, Thus saith the LORD, Even by the young men of the princes of the provinces. Then he said, Who shall order the battle? And he answered, Thou.

modern.text: “By whom?” Ahab asked. And the prophet replied, “This is what the LORD says: ‘By the young officers of the district governors.’” “Who will start the battle?” asked Ahab. “You will,” answered the prophet.

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אַחְאָב֙ בְּמִ֔י וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ כֹּֽה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה בְּנַעֲרֵ֖י שָׂרֵ֣י הַמְּדִינ֑וֹת וַיֹּ֛אמֶר מִֽי יֶאְסֹ֥ר הַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אָֽתָּה

verses.restored: He counted young men of provincial officials, two hundred thirty-two. After them he counted all people, all children of Israel, seven thousand.

familiar.text: Then he numbered the young men of the princes of the provinces, and they were two hundred and thirty two: and after them he numbered all the people, even all the children of Israel, being seven thousand.

modern.text: So Ahab assembled the young officers of the district governors, and there were 232 men. And after them, he assembled the rest of the Israelite troops, 7,000 in all.

original.text: וַיִּפְקֹ֗ד אֶֽת נַעֲרֵי֙ שָׂרֵ֣י הַמְּדִינ֔וֹת וַיִּהְי֕וּ מָאתַ֖יִם שְׁנַ֣יִם וּשְׁלֹשִׁ֑ים וְאַחֲרֵיהֶ֗ם פָּקַ֧ד אֶת כָּל הָעָ֛ם כָּל בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל שִׁבְעַ֥ת אֲלָפִֽים

verses.restored: They went out at noon while Ben-hadad was drinking himself drunk in shelters, he and thirty-two kings helping him.

familiar.text: And they went out at noon. But Benhadad was drinking himself drunk in the pavilions, he and the kings, the thirty and two kings that helped him.

modern.text: They marched out at noon while Ben-hadad and the 32 kings allied with him were in their tents getting drunk.

original.text: וַיֵּצְא֖וּ בַּֽצָּהֳרָ֑יִם וּבֶן הֲדַד֩ שֹׁתֶ֨ה שִׁכּ֜וֹר בַּסֻּכּ֗וֹת ה֧וּא וְהַמְּלָכִ֛ים שְׁלֹשִֽׁים וּשְׁנַ֥יִם מֶ֖לֶךְ עֹזֵ֥ר אֹתֽוֹ

verses.restored: Young men of provincial officials went out first. Ben-hadad sent, and they told him, Men came out from Samaria.

familiar.text: And the young men of the princes of the provinces went out first; and Benhadad sent out, and they told him, saying, There are men come out of Samaria.

modern.text: And the young officers of the district governors marched out first. Now Ben-hadad had sent out scouts, who reported to him, “Men are marching out of Samaria.”

original.text: וַיֵּצְא֗וּ נַעֲרֵ֛י שָׂרֵ֥י הַמְּדִינ֖וֹת בָּרִֽאשֹׁנָ֑ה וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח בֶּן הֲדַ֗ד וַיַּגִּ֤ידוּ לוֹ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר אֲנָשִׁ֕ים יָצְא֖וּ מִשֹּׁמְרֽוֹן

verses.restored: He said, If for peace they came, seize them alive; if for battle they came, seize them alive.

familiar.text: And he said, Whether they be come out for peace, take them alive; or whether they be come out for war, take them alive.

modern.text: “If they have marched out in peace,” he said, “take them alive. Even if they have marched out for war, take them alive.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֛אמֶר אִם לְשָׁל֥וֹם יָצָ֖אוּ תִּפְשׂ֣וּם חַיִּ֑ים וְאִ֧ם לְמִלְחָמָ֛ה יָצָ֖אוּ חַיִּ֥ים תִּפְשֽׂוּם

verses.restored: These young men of provincial officials went out from city, and army followed them.

familiar.text: So these young men of the princes of the provinces came out of the city, and the army which followed them.

modern.text: Meanwhile, these young officers of the district governors marched out of the city, with the army behind them,

original.text: וְאֵ֨לֶּה֙ יָצְא֣וּ מִן הָעִ֔יר נַעֲרֵ֖י שָׂרֵ֣י הַמְּדִינ֑וֹת וְהַחַ֖יִל אֲשֶׁ֥ר אַחֲרֵיהֶֽם

verses.restored: Each struck his man. Arameans fled, and Israel pursued them. Ben-hadad king of Aram escaped upon horse with horsemen.

familiar.text: And they slew every one his man: and the Syrians fled; and Israel pursued them: and Benhadad the king of Syria escaped on an horse with the horsemen.

modern.text: and each one struck down his opponent. So the Arameans fled, with the Israelites in pursuit. But Ben-hadad king of Aram escaped on horseback with the cavalry.

original.text: וַיַּכּוּ֙ אִ֣ישׁ אִישׁ֔וֹ וַיָּנֻ֣סוּ אֲרָ֔ם וַֽיִּרְדְּפֵ֖ם יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיִּמָּלֵ֗ט בֶּן הֲדַד֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ אֲרָ֔ם עַל ס֖וּס וּפָרָשִֽׁים

verses.restored: King of Israel went out, struck horses and chariots, and struck Aram with a great blow/slaughter.

familiar.text: And the king of Israel went out, and smote the horses and chariots, and slew the Syrians with a great slaughter.

modern.text: Then the king of Israel marched out and attacked the horses and chariots, inflicting a great slaughter on the Arameans.

original.text: וַיֵּצֵא֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיַּ֥ךְ אֶת הַסּ֖וּס וְאֶת הָרָ֑כֶב וְהִכָּ֥ה בַאֲרָ֖ם מַכָּ֥ה גְדוֹלָֽה

verses.restored: The prophet came near king of Israel and said, Go, strengthen yourself, know and see what you shall do, for at turn of year king of Aram will come up against you.

familiar.text: And the prophet came to the king of Israel, and said unto him, Go, strengthen thyself, and mark, and see what thou doest: for at the return of the year the king of Syria will come up against thee.

modern.text: Afterward, the prophet approached the king of Israel and said, “Go and strengthen your position, and take note what you must do, for in the spring the king of Aram will come up against you.”

original.text: וַיִּגַּ֤שׁ הַנָּבִיא֙ אֶל מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ לֵ֣ךְ הִתְחַזַּ֔ק וְדַ֥ע וּרְאֵ֖ה אֵ֣ת אֲשֶֽׁר תַּעֲשֶׂ֑ה כִּ֚י לִתְשׁוּבַ֣ת הַשָּׁנָ֔ה מֶ֥לֶךְ אֲרָ֖ם עֹלֶ֥ה עָלֶֽיךָ

verses.restored: Servants of king of Aram said, Their gods are gods of mountains; therefore they were stronger than we. But let us fight them in plain; surely we shall be stronger.

familiar.text: And the servants of the king of Syria said unto him, Their gods are gods of the hills; therefore they were stronger than we; but let us fight against them in the plain, and surely we shall be stronger than they.

modern.text: Meanwhile, the servants of the king of Aram said to him, “Their gods are gods of the hills. That is why they prevailed over us. Instead, we should fight them on the plains; surely then we will prevail.

original.text: וְעַבְדֵ֨י מֶֽלֶךְ אֲרָ֜ם אָמְר֣וּ אֵלָ֗יו אֱלֹהֵ֤י הָרִים֙ אֱלֹ֣הֵיהֶ֔ם עַל כֵּ֖ן חָזְק֣וּ מִמֶּ֑נּוּ וְאוּלָ֗ם נִלָּחֵ֤ם אִתָּם֙ בַּמִּישׁ֔וֹר אִם לֹ֥א נֶחֱזַ֖ק מֵהֶֽם

verses.restored: Do this matter: remove kings each from his place and put governors in their places.

familiar.text: And do this thing, Take the kings away, every man out of his place, and put captains in their rooms:

modern.text: So do this: Dismiss all the kings from their positions and replace them with other officers.

original.text: וְאֶת הַדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּ֖ה עֲשֵׂ֑ה הָסֵ֤ר הַמְּלָכִים֙ אִ֣ישׁ מִמְּקֹמ֔וֹ וְשִׂ֥ים פַּח֖וֹת תַּחְתֵּיהֶֽם

familiar.text: And number thee an army, like the army that thou hast lost, horse for horse, and chariot for chariot: and we will fight against them in the plain, and surely we shall be stronger than they. And he hearkened unto their voice, and did so.

modern.text: And you must raise an army like the one you have lost—horse for horse and chariot for chariot—so we can fight the Israelites on the plain, where we will surely prevail.” And the king approved their plan and acted accordingly. Another War with Ben-hadad

modern.text: Then the man of God approached the king of Israel and said, “This is what the LORD says: ‘Because the Arameans think the LORD is a god of the hills and not of the valleys, I will deliver all this great army into your hand. Then you will know that I am the LORD.’”

translation_notes: Ben-hadad treats silver, gold, wives, and children as possessions transferable from one king to another. Women and children are hostages and persons, never royal property.
Ahab initially agrees to surrender his household and wealth before resisting the invasive search. His eventual boundary does not erase his willingness to assign other people's lives.
Ben-hadad's intoxication occurs during military command, but alcohol should not become an ethnic or moral stereotype or excuse for Israel's slaughter.
Young provincial attendants lead the attack. Youth language must not romanticize child soldiers or pressure inexperienced people into combat.

The reported one hundred thousand deaths and wall killing twenty-seven thousand require textual, rhetorical, and historical audit; ancient battle numbers may be hyperbolic and must not become celebratory statistics.
Aramean claims about mountain and valley gods are wartime religious interpretation. They do not justify contempt toward Arameans or other religions.

Ben-hadad negotiates survival, restoration of cities, and trade rights. Mercy toward a captive is not inherently sinful, even though political accountability and protection of victims remain necessary.

A prophet orders a companion to strike him; refusal is followed by death from a lion. This sacred-violence story must not be used to coerce assault, punish conscientious refusal, or treat animals as execution tools.
The final oracle uses herem—devotion to destruction—to condemn Ahab for releasing Ben-hadad. It must not teach that mercy is disobedience or that captives should be executed.
Ahab's covenant with Ben-hadad may be politically self-serving, but ethical critique should focus on justice, restitution, and future safety rather than demanding killing.
safety_note: Do not treat wives, children, captives, or cities as royal property. Do not glorify casualty totals, coerce someone to strike another person, or teach that mercy deserves punishment. Reject herem as a modern policy; pursue accountable peace, restitution, due process, and protection of civilians.
